candidate_name: Côte d'Ivoire–Benin–Togo regional pooled-LNG-import hub (World Bank framework)
sponsor_or_proposer: Governments of Côte d'Ivoire, Benin and Togo (energy ministries); World Bank Group (backer/facilitator). No commercial terminal sponsor named yet.
current_state: Framework/pre-feasibility only. On 9 Dec 2025 the three countries' energy ministers signed a joint declaration in Abidjan, backed by the World Bank, to pool LNG imports regionally. Declaration priorities: (1) pool LNG imports, (2) stand up a technical working group within one month to design an operating model, (3) develop a 'bankable project structure' with World Bank assistance. No terminal, FSRU, host site, capacity, or commercial sponsor has been named; no FID/FEED/MOU/site-selection for a specific facility.
missing_threshold_elements: sponsor (no commercial terminal sponsor — only governments + World Bank as facilitator); location (host country/port for the pooled import point not selected — could be Abidjan, Lomé, or Cotonou); concrete step (only a framework declaration + intent to form a working group; no site selection, FEED, permit, or charter for a specific terminal)
watch_for: Designation of a host country/port for the pooled import terminal; an FSRU charter or operator tender tied to the trilateral framework; World Bank/IFC project-appraisal or financing document naming a specific terminal; whether the hub revives the shelved Abidjan/Vridi FSRU (GEM T100000130835) rather than a greenfield site. Note: a parallel Benin FSRU lead may surface in the Benin discovery file.
notes: Forward signal, not yet a project. Re-verified 2026-06-04 with two independent non-GEM reports of the same 9 Dec 2025 trilateral ministerial declaration: Ecofin Agency (PASS on 'LNG'+'Togo') and African Energy (PASS on 'gas import'). No gem.wiki/globalenergymonitor.org citation involved — anti-circularity holds (conclusion rests on the two primary press reports, not on any GEM-derived restatement). The country may host the pooled import point given Abidjan was the meeting venue and CIV already has the shelved Vridi FSRU, but the declaration commits no site. Re-check ~mid-2026 once the technical working group reports. Note: a Togo First report of the same declaration (togofirst.com/en/energy/0812-17753) was attempted as a third corroboration but failed url_verifier (HTTP 000 — host blocks the fetch), so it is not cited.
